newsitem.title: USA: Dow costs rose in Q4, but volume also rose.
newsitem.headline: Dow costs rose in Q4, but volume also rose.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co said Thursday feedstock and energy costs continued to rise in the fourth quarter, but said it substantially offset the combined impact of $475 million in lower prices and higher costs.
The company reported fourth quarter earnings of $1.69 per share on $4.9 billion in sales. Wall Street had expected earnings of $1.62, according to a First Call consensus estimate.

Dow said a 10 percent increase in volume offset a three percent price decline during the fourth quarter. The company said prices were off for some key products, particularly caustic and polystyrene, but that notable exceptions were polyethylene and vinyl chloride monomer, whose prices rose modestly.
It said plastics had the sharpest rise in volume, posting gains of 21 percent for the quarter and a full-year increase of 17 percent above the 1995 figures.

Chemicals and metals had a volume gain of 12 percent in the quarter, based largely on strong demand for vinyl chloride monomer, the company said. It added that agricultural chemicals experienced particularly strong demand in Latin America and Asia Pacific due to new product introductions like CLINCHER rice herbicide.

The company said its performance segments generated close to 50 percent of its sales and over half of its operating income for the year. Sales in 1996 were basically flat with 1995, but operating income rose eight percent for performance chemicals and 11 percent for performance plastics, Dow said.
